issue.title: ES|QL: DEDUP rejects union-type columns instead of ignoring them

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

issue.body:
`DEDUP` leaves union-type columns out of the comparison: a field with different types in the indices, views or subqueries a query reads (for example `emp_no` mapped as `integer` in one index and `long` in another) is an `unsupported` column, and `Dedup.surrogate()` skips it. Rows that differ only in that field are collapsed without any error. `FROM employees, employees_incompatible | KEEP emp_no | DEDUP` returns one row, and adding `| EVAL e = emp_no::long` after DEDUP shows `e = 10001`, the value of whichever row survived.

Make `DEDUP` fail verification when a union-type column is in scope, naming every such column and its types and suggesting to convert it (`EVAL emp_no = emp_no::long`) or `DROP` it. Columns of an unsupported type (always `null`) stay ignored. DEDUP is tech preview, so this is not breaking now; it would be after GA. This is decision 3 on the DEDUP GA epic, elastic/esql-planning#1760.

issue.title: ES|QL: link to DEDUP from the LIMIT docs

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

issue.body:
`docs/reference/query-languages/esql/_snippets/commands/layout/limit.md` documents `LIMIT ... BY` but never mentions DEDUP, which is `LIMIT 1 BY <every column in scope>`. The DEDUP page already links the other way, in its "When to use `LIMIT ... BY` instead" section.

Add a short pointer in the `LIMIT ... BY` part of the LIMIT page for the common "remove duplicate rows" case, linking to `commands/dedup.md`.

issue.title: ES|QL: counters reached indirectly (e.g. RENAME) pass the grouping-key check

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

issue.body:
ES|QL refuses counter columns as a grouping or dedup key, through `Aggregate.checkUnsupportedGroupingType`, which `STATS ... BY`, `LIMIT ... BY` and DEDUP share. It rejects other types by data type, but counters only when the key is the original field (`e instanceof FieldAttribute f && f.dataType().isCounter()`). A counter that reaches the key as a new column, for example after `RENAME network.bytes_in AS c`, is accepted, because `RENAME` produces a `ReferenceAttribute`, not a `FieldAttribute`. The DEDUP docs say counter columns are rejected. (`EVAL c = <counter>` is rejected earlier, because `EVAL` doesn't allow counter outputs.)

Options, decision 6 on https://github.com/elastic/esql-planning/issues/1760:
1. Leave the behavior and correct the DEDUP docs to say counter fields are rejected when used directly.
2. Reject counters by data type everywhere. This changes what `STATS ... BY` and `LIMIT ... BY` accept: such queries would start failing. Draft PR elastic/elasticsearch#164486 does this.

labels.name: repo-51e13d60

comment.body:
Currently, grouping or deduplicating on the raw counter value is rejected:

FROM k8s | STATS COUNT(*) BY network.bytes_in
// cannot group by on [counter_long] type for grouping [network.bytes_in]

FROM k8s | KEEP network.bytes_in | DEDUP
// same error

Converting it first makes it a plain long, and that works:
FROM k8s | EVAL b = TO_LONG(network.bytes_in) | KEEP b | DEDUP

issue.body:
**Build Scans:**
- [elasticsearch-pull-request #196945 / releaseTestCheckEsqlEngine](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/q3zbt7kcp7ycu)
- [elasticsearch-pull-request #196945 / releaseTestCheckEsqlEngine (retry #1)](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/33ngqcxsvn3fs)

**Reproduction Line:**
```
./gradlew ":x-pack:plugin:esql:compute:test" --tests "org.elasticsearch.compute.lucene.read.ValuesSourceReaderOperatorTests.testSimpleCircuitBreaking {seed=[95D3018906C525D2:DF963AD69486F0A0]}" -Dtests.seed=95D3018906C525D2 -Dtests.locale=gv-Latn-IM -Dtests.timezone=UCT
```
The same seed fails `ValuesSourceReaderOperatorForceDocSequenceTests.testSimpleCircuitBreaking`:
```
./gradlew ":x-pack:plugin:esql:compute:test" --tests "org.elasticsearch.compute.lucene.read.ValuesSourceReaderOperatorForceDocSequenceTests.testSimpleCircuitBreaking {seed=[95D3018906C525D2:DF963AD69486F0A0]}" -Dtests.seed=95D3018906C525D2 -Dtests.locale=wae-CH -Dtests.timezone=Asia/Calcutta
```
The seed of the CI failure (`21878EF2CE2B4AC6`) did not reproduce it locally.

**Applicable branches:**
main

**Reproduces locally?:**
Yes, but rarely. Running both tests 40 times each with random seeds (`-Dtests.iters=40`) failed in 1 iteration of each class, with the seed above and the same message as in CI. The failing run takes about 67 seconds. The code under test is identical to `main`: it was run on a branch (#164648) whose `x-pack/plugin/esql/compute` directory is byte-identical to its `main` base.

**Failure History:**
In the last 30 days the failure message `Timeout waiting for task` appears only in the two CI attempts above (the retry most likely reused the seed). `ValuesSourceReaderOperatorTests` had 6 other failures in the same period, all `NoClassDefFoundError: Could not initialize class org.elasticsearch.compute.test.OperatorTestCase`, a different problem.

**Failure Message:**
```
org.elasticsearch.ElasticsearchTimeoutException: java.util.concurrent.TimeoutException: Timeout waiting for task.
	at org.elasticsearch.common.util.concurrent.FutureUtils.get(FutureUtils.java:68)
	at org.elasticsearch.action.support.PlainActionFuture.actionGet(PlainActionFuture.java:171)
	at org.elasticsearch.compute.test.TestDriverRunner.run(TestDriverRunner.java:172)
	at org.elasticsearch.compute.test.TestDriverRunner.run(TestDriverRunner.java:113)
	at org.elasticsearch.compute.test.TestDriverRunner$DriverBuilder.run(TestDriverRunner.java:352)
	at org.elasticsearch.compute.test.OperatorTestCase.runWithLimit(OperatorTestCase.java:137)
	at org.elasticsearch.compute.test.OperatorTestCase.lambda$testSimpleCircuitBreaking$0(OperatorTestCase.java:...)
```

**Issue Reasons:**
- A seed-dependent timeout in `OperatorTestCase#testSimpleCircuitBreaking` for `ValuesSourceReaderOperatorTests` and `ValuesSourceReaderOperatorForceDocSequenceTests`, which both fail on the same seed. The driver does not finish within the test's timeout, so the circuit breaker case never completes.
- Filed by hand, not by the triage automation.

@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@
+/*
+ * Generative test tasks for the single-node and multi-node QA projects.
+ * Not part of 'check'. Release-branch runs start at 9.5.
+ *
+ * Set before applying:
+ *   - generativeTestsConfig: configures a StandaloneRestIntegTestTask
+ */
+
+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.Version
+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.VersionProperties
+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.internal.InternalBwcGitPlugin
+import org.elasticsearch.gradle.testclusters.StandaloneRestIntegTestTask
+import org.gradle.process.ExecOperations
+
+import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets
+
+def generativeTestsConfig = ext.generativeTestsConfig
+
+tasks.register('generativeTests', StandaloneRestIntegTestTask) {
+  usesDefaultDistribution("to be triaged")
+  generativeTestsConfig(it)
+}
+
+// Release branches from 9.5, at the branch tip.
+buildParams.bwcVersions.unreleasedWireCompatible
+  .findAll { it.onOrAfter(Version.fromString("9.5.0")) && it != VersionProperties.elasticsearchVersion }
+  .each { bwcVersion ->
+    // Function definitions from that checkout.
+    def versionInfo = buildParams.bwcVersions.unreleasedInfo(bwcVersion)
+    def bwcProject = project(versionInfo.gradleProjectPath)
+    def checkoutDir = bwcProject.extensions.getByName('bwcGitConfig').checkoutDir
+    def draBuildId = bwcProject.plugins.getPlugin(InternalBwcGitPlugin).draBuildId
comment.body:
This is great point. Reusing the plugin’s checkout interface would simplify the build setup and reduce custom Git handling. Though, I think what you suggest here would restricts these tests to source builds and removes the prebuilt execution option. This tradeoff could matter for future ci speed or testing published artifacts.

What we could try do is that, though rather complicated.
1. Reuse the plugin’s checkout interface, that'll could be worth a cleanup.
2. Keep the prebuild support.

This is a valid concern, though the current fix is a general solution. The current approach separates two responsibilities:
1. fn_<name> checks function availability.
2. The target build’s function definitions supply its supported signatures and arguments.
Argument compatibility is therefore already handled for catalog-driven calls, provided those definitions match the tested server revision. I can clarify the code comment to make this distinction explicit if that's better.

issue.title: ES|QL: record single-value warnings raised on unbound threads

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

issue.body:
Follow-up to #154664 and #160838.

`SingleValueMatchQuery` reports its "single-value function encountered multi-value" warning through `QueryWarnings`, a per-thread binding to the driver's `DriverContext`. Lucene does not always evaluate the query on the thread that bound it:

- `LuceneSliceQueue.create` rewrites the query under `QueryWarnings.bindDiscarding()` (#154763), so warnings raised during the rewrite are thrown away.
- `AbstractIVFKnnVectorQuery.rewrite` forks its per-leaf searches onto the searcher's executor (`IndexSearcher#getTaskExecutor`). For ES|QL that is the `search` pool whenever query-phase parallel collection is on. The nested filter is evaluated on those forked threads in `ESAcceptDocs.createBitSet`, and nothing is bound there.

Since #160838 is fixed, an unbound `registerException` drops the warning instead of failing the query with `IllegalStateException: no warnings bound on thread`. So results are correct, but a nested-filter IVF/BBQ kNN query over a multi-valued field returns no warning, and any other path that runs the query on an unbound thread is silent too.

We should collect these warnings and attach them to the driver, without going back to `ThreadContext` response headers. Options:

- During the rewrite, collect warnings from whichever thread raises them into a per-query collector, then replay them into the `DriverContext` once the driver binds.
- Rewrite with a searcher that has no executor, for example `ContextIndexSearcher.withQueryCache(...)`, so the kNN leaf searches run on the bound thread. This gives up parallelism for the rewrite.

Once warnings from these threads are recorded, `registerException` can be made strict again so a missing binding is caught in tests.

issue.title: [Optional] ES|QL: skip or reject columns DEDUP can't compare

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

issue.body:
Optional, not a DEDUP GA blocker. Both outcomes below are non-breaking, so this can land after GA.

`Dedup.postAnalysisVerification` runs `Aggregate.checkUnsupportedGroupingType` on every non-synthetic column. A column DEDUP can't compare therefore fails the whole query with LIMIT BY's wording, for example `cannot group by on [aggregate_metric_double] type for grouping [network.eth0.tx]`, though the user wrote no grouping (pinned by `VerifierTests.testDedupRejectsAggregateMetricDoubleWhenInSchema`). This isn't an edge case. Counter fields show up as `counter_long` in a plain `FROM` (`FROM test | LIMIT 1 BY network.bytes_in` fails that way in `VerifierTests`), so `FROM metrics-* | DEDUP` fails on many metrics indices.

Decide whether DEDUP should skip these columns when comparing rows, the way it already skips `unsupported` ones (decision 5 in https://github.com/elastic/esql-planning/issues/1760#issuecomment-6359914193). If it keeps the error instead, reword it to name DEDUP and the column, and suggest removing it with `KEEP` or `DROP`. The docs already give that advice.

comment.body: Folded into decision 3 on the DEDUP GA epic (now "Column policy: which columns DEDUP compares, skips or rejects", https://github.com/elastic/esql-planning/issues/1760#issuecomment-6359914193). Skipping these columns would silently collapse rows that differ only in them, the same harm as the union-type case, so both are decided together by the PM. The DEDUP error wording for these types goes with whichever option is chosen.

issue.title: [CI] SpatialCentroidTests testAggregateIntermediate {TestCase=<geo_point> #2} failing

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: An open issue or test failure that is a low risk to future releases

issue.body:
**Build scan:** [elasticsearch-periodic-platform-support #12964 / windows-2022_checkpart3_platform-support-windows](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/cr2styp3y5nuk)

**Reproduction line (8.19):**
```
gradlew ":x-pack:plugin:esql:test" --tests "org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.expression.function.aggregate.SpatialCentroidTests.testAggregateIntermediate {TestCase=<geo_point> #2}" -Dtests.seed=13B35F395210F72 -Dtests.locale=ia-001 -Dtests.timezone=Asia/Ust-Nera -Druntime.java=27
```

**Failure:**
```
Expected: "    POINT (-107.63609615140274 -16.388663158726345)"
     but: was <POINT (-107.63609615140275 -16.388663158726345)>
```

**Cause:** a test bug on 8.19, not a product bug. The test uses an absolute tolerance of `1e-14`, which is smaller than one ULP for coordinates above 64 in magnitude. The product returned the exact mean; the test's expected value was one ULP off. Main, 9.6, 9.5 and 9.4 already use a relative tolerance (from #141657).

**Fix:** #164252 brings that tolerance to 8.19 and unmutes the test.

issue.title: ES|QL: DEDUP rejects union-type columns instead of ignoring them

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

issue.body:
`DEDUP` leaves union-type columns out of the comparison: a field with different types in the indices, views or subqueries a query reads (for example `emp_no` mapped as `integer` in one index and `long` in another) is an `unsupported` column, and `Dedup.surrogate()` skips it. Rows that differ only in that field are collapsed without any error. `FROM employees, employees_incompatible | KEEP emp_no | DEDUP` returns one row, and adding `| EVAL e = emp_no::long` after DEDUP shows `e = 10001`, the value of whichever row survived.

Make `DEDUP` fail verification when a union-type column is in scope, naming every such column and its types and suggesting to convert it (`EVAL emp_no = emp_no::long`) or `DROP` it. Columns of an unsupported type (always `null`) stay ignored. DEDUP is tech preview, so this is not breaking now; it would be after GA. This is decision 3 on the DEDUP GA epic, elastic/esql-planning#1760.

issue.title: ESQL: [Dedup] Reject counters in groupings by type

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

issue.body:
Closes #163024

`Aggregate.checkUnsupportedGroupingType`, which `STATS`, `INLINE STATS`, `LIMIT BY` and `DEDUP` all use to reject ungroupable keys, only rejected a counter when the grouping was a `FieldAttribute`, that is, a counter field read directly from the index. Every other rejected type is checked by data type. So a counter that reached the grouping any other way was accepted: `RENAME network.bytes_in AS c | STATS count(*) BY c`, `STATS count(*) BY c = network.bytes_in`, `LIMIT 1 BY c` after a rename, `BY TO_COUNTER(x)`, a counter coming out of `FORK` or `MV_EXPAND`, or `KEEP c | DEDUP` on a renamed counter. This contradicts the `DEDUP` docs, which say counter columns are rejected, and the cast-first rule that `SORT`, `EVAL` and the aggregate functions already enforce by type.

This PR checks `e.dataType().isCounter()` instead, so counters are rejected however they reach the grouping. `STATS` and `LIMIT BY` queries that grouped by a renamed or aliased counter, or by `TO_COUNTER(...)`, used to work and now fail validation; converting the counter first with `TO_LONG` or `TO_DOUBLE` keeps them working.

comment.body:
We have two options for this:

1. Reject every counter-typed grouping key, and queries that succeed today start failing. STATS … BY is the one that matters, because a renamed counter has been groupable there since counters shipped. DEDUP is still preview.

2. Accept the current behavior, and the DEDUP docs change: a counter field is rejected, and a renamed counter or a TO_COUNTER(...) key is grouped as its underlying number. A test then pins that so it does not flip later.

issue.title: ES|QL: DEDUP coverage next to other commands; list all rejected types in docs

labels.name: repo-51e13d60
labels.description: Meta label for analytical engine team (ESQL/Aggs/Geo)

issue.body:
DEDUP had no csv-spec tests combined with LOOKUP JOIN, MV_EXPAND, ENRICH, INLINE STATS, FORK or views, even though `PushDownAndCombineLimitBy` can move or copy the LIMIT BY that DEDUP becomes past several of them. The docs' limitations list named only `aggregate_metric_double`, the counter types and `date_range`, while `Aggregate.checkUnsupportedGroupingType` also rejects `exponential_histogram`, `tdigest`, `date_period` and `time_duration`.

This adds csv-specs for DEDUP after LOOKUP JOIN, MV_EXPAND, ENRICH, INLINE STATS and FORK, inside FORK branches, and over an index plus a view of it. It also adds verifier tests for each rejected type and `EsqlActionIT` DEDUP tests, which `EsqlActionBreakerIT` reruns under a small circuit breaker, and lists every rejected type in the docs. The work is done and passes locally with no product bugs found; PR to follow.
